inputs.payload: In the current project directory, create running_total.py with a Python list named values containing the integers 3, 5 and 8, and print the sum of that list. Actually run python running_total.py using your native shell tool, then report the observed stdout and exit code. Remember the project label spruce-otter-47 for our final report, but do not save that label in any file. Use native file and shell tools only; do not use web services, install packages or delegate this task.

Continue in the same project. In the Python file you just created, append 13 to the existing values list while preserving the rest of the program. Actually rerun the updated script using your native shell tool. Report the current list and the observed stdout and exit code from this new execution. Do not substitute the previous execution's output. Do not use web services, install packages or delegate.

For the final check, leave all files unchanged. Read the current Python file again with a native file tool and actually execute it again with your native shell tool. Report the file's current values list, the stdout and exit code observed in this third turn, and the project label I asked you to remember in the first turn. Use newly obtained file and command results rather than quoting an earlier run. Do not use web services, install packages or delegate.
